properties.value: A router may serve any model in the request's equiv_class, but only when the request carries downgrade_ok; anything else is a typed substitution violation. Quality is booked from the model actually served, not the one requested.
properties.tradeoff: Substituting outside {model_requested} u (equiv_class if downgrade_ok) is a hard fail; both tenants ship downgrade_ok: true, so all 12 models are legally reachable. The served model's ground-truth score is what counts toward mean_quality.

properties.value: Placement is free among the providers that stock the chosen model; price, latency and quota headroom differ by provider and the fleet view publishes all three live, by value.
properties.tradeoff: Dispatching to an unknown provider or to a provider that does not stock the model is a typed violation and the request is NOT retried automatically: the harness returns without rescheduling, so the request is lost unless the router acts again.

properties.value: Refusing a request is legal only under real overload: no non-down provider stocking a legally substitutable model may have rpm, tpm AND concurrency headroom at that instant.
properties.tradeoff: An illegal shed is a typed illegal_shed violation; a legal shed still books zero quality, a quality-floor miss, and counts as an SLO-violated request in the tenant's rate. Shedding is therefore never a cheap way to improve any scored axis.

properties.value: Each provider enforces a 60 s sliding request window, a 60 s token window and a standing concurrency cap; exceeding any of them returns 429 with a fixed 2000 ms retry-after, and the token window is charged prompt_tokens + expected_output_tokens.
properties.tradeoff: The fleet view publishes rpm_left and tpm_left but NOT the concurrency cap; inflight is published and the cap is public static spec in the env card. prime is sized so bursts genuinely saturate it: rpm 132, tpm 3.5M, concurrency 32, against value's rpm 420 / concurrency 96.

properties.value: The harness itself reschedules a rejected request: on 429/503 it calls on_error and pushes a wake event at now + retry_after, so decide() is re-invoked and the router chooses again from scratch.
properties.tradeoff: A rejected attempt is never billed (the bill is charged only inside a successful admit), and a request may be attempted any number of times, but exactly one completion is ever booked; a second completion is a typed double_bill.

properties.value: An outage is ANNOUNCED, not inferred: a down provider publishes an empty model catalogue plus an outage_until ETA in the fleet view, and admits nothing.
properties.tradeoff: Dispatching into an announced outage more than retry_grace = 8 times loses the request with a typed outage_lost violation. Validation outage windows are literal in the card (300-420 s and 780-930 s on prime); test windows are derived from test_seed at replay time and must not be inspected.

properties.value: Each request carries exactly one SLO field and the harness measures the matching quantity: slo.latency_ms is checked against whole-response time from arrival, slo.ttft_ms against arrival-to-first-token measured directly at dispatch.
properties.tradeoff: Tenant A is ttft_ms = 2500 and Tenant B is latency_ms = 600000, so the same fleet must be treated as two different scheduling problems. A request that never completes (shed, lost or dead) is counted as SLO-violated in the tenant rate.

properties.value: The harness tags each trace row with its tenant and keeps a separate book per tenant (requests, completed, shed, quality, cost, SLO violations, throttles, outage rejects). The tenant is not a Router.decide() argument, but every trace row's observable features map carries a tenant key, so a router CAN read it from the request it is handed.
properties.tradeoff: Each tenant is scored separately against the same generic baseline, so the specialist must win on ITS tenant's book; the merged-traffic contention is real because both tenants replay against one shared set of provider counters.

properties.value: Cost is billed by the harness from its own private price table as (fresh*in + cached*cached + expected_output*out)/1e6, tallied independently, and cross-checked at end of run.
properties.tradeoff: The bill can never be below the all-cached floor (typed bad_bill), the fleet's price tables are published by value so a router editing them edits only its own copy (typed env_mutation / meter_mutation tripwires), and cost carries weight 3.0 in the declared utility.

properties.value: The router keeps whatever state it likes on self, but the harness hands it a COPY of each request with stable identity across decide/on_error/on_complete, diffs that copy against truth after every callback, and rolls back any edit.
properties.tradeoff: Editing a trace field is a typed req_mutation; any exception out of a callback is a typed router_exception and the replay still closes its books. Liveness is bounded at 512 decide() calls per request and 600 s wall clock, and deferring a structurally unservable request more than 32 times is a typed unserviceable loss.

properties.value: The router reports nothing: every scored number (billing, token counts, SLO accounting, quality) is read from harness truth, and the replay emits per-tenant books, typed violation kinds and per-provider leading indicators.
properties.tradeoff: Nothing a router returns or logs can move the score, so self-reported metrics are for the operator only; the first 20 violations plus a full violation-kind histogram are the operator-visible failure signal.
